source.description:
PROBLEM
Operator review 2026-09-08, from a real coordinator session, raised six friction points. Three are fixed; these three are not, and they are the ones that cost the most.

1. NO BUILD IDENTITY ON THE SURFACE (this is unitAI-rrdnt.55's shape, sharpened). The operator's only way to tell a stale runtime from broken input was to DIFF THE TOOL DESCRIPTION against source — the loaded copy lacked a sentence the on-disk file had. That tell is discoverable only by reading the repo. Nothing in dispatch or status exposes which build is loaded.
Suggested shape, which satisfies .55's constraint without per-call imports: surface a stable build identity in specialist_status and annex it to every rejection — 'module loaded <id>, dist on disk <id>'. When they differ, say so IN THE REFUSAL. One refusal with two causes is exactly where messages lie, and this session proved it.

2. THE LEASE IS UNEXPLAINED TO THE CALLER. 'Workspace lease' appears in refusals with no statement of what it is, how to check availability, or that it is held for the duration of a turn. A coordinator meeting workspace_held_by_another_writer has no model of what to do next.

3. LATENCY IS UNSTATED. Descriptions say to check status without any sense of the per-turn budget the runtime comments measure (~1-2 min). Absent that, a coordinator either polls hot or assumes a hang.

ALSO RAISED, and worth doing together with the above: tool descriptions mix operating instructions with PRD rationale (VALIDATION 5, .44/.48 cross-refs). For source readers that is valuable; as model-facing text it competes with the instructions. Keep one 'why' line per tool, move the rest to docs.

SUCCESS
A coordinator meeting a refusal can tell a stale build from a bad contract without reading source, knows what a workspace lease is and how long one is held, and has a latency expectation. Tool descriptions carry operating instructions plus at most one line of rationale.

SCRUTINY
LOW

SCOPE
config/pi-extensions/specialist-subagents/index.mjs and src/tools/specialist/activation.tool.ts descriptions and refusal rendering; whatever computes the build identity.

NON_GOALS
Does not change admission, the gate, or the lease itself. Does not import dist per call — unitAI-rrdnt.55 rules that out and the reasoning stands.

CONSTRAINTS
Build identity must be cheap at load and STABLE across identical builds — a timestamp changes every rebuild and would make two identical builds look different. The config fingerprint the runtime already computes is the closer precedent.
Both frontends must say the same thing. Divergent wording between them is the defect recorded in .55 and .56.

VALIDATION
1. A coordinator running a stale build against a valid contract gets a refusal that names staleness as a candidate cause.
2. Both frontends carry identical lease and latency wording.

OUTPUT
The build identity, the refusal annotation, and the trimmed descriptions.

REFERENCES
Operator review 2026-09-08. Already fixed from the same review: the accepted heading forms (unitAI-rrdnt.54), the SCRUTINY level list and the eight-not-seven correction (unitAI-rrdnt.57), created_bead_id plus a lifecycle note on inline dispatch, and a routing line to `sp run <name> --prompt` for untracked one-offs.
source.notes:
Taken with unitAI-rrdnt.55 as one tranche by the pi-specialists coordinator, 2026-09-08. .60 subsumes .55 fix; do them as one change. dawid-0b is not working these.
OWNERSHIP CORRECTION 2026-09-08 — this bead was assigned in error and is UNOWNED again.

I assigned it to 'pi-specialists' on the strength of a peer message saying that session was taking .55/.60 as a tranche. The session then corrected me: the activation I was talking to is a READ-ONLY explorer (bead unitAI-v29bw, boundary rules explorer-readonly) with no bd tooling and no mutation surface. It could not have claimed a bead, could not write to one, and cannot do this work from inside that activation.

So I recorded an owner who was structurally incapable of being one, and had the peer not flagged it, .55 and .60 would have sat idle looking owned. That is worse than unowned: an unowned bead gets picked up, an incorrectly-owned one does not.

MY ERROR, precisely: I treated a peer's statement of intent as a durable ownership fact and wrote it to the board without verifying the session could act on it. Assignment is board state and should follow evidence, not a message. The peer caught it and called it a coordination hazard rather than a detail, which is the right severity.

These need a fresh WRITE-CAPABLE tracked activation, dispatched as one change (.60 subsumes .55's fix).
ANNEX POINT PINNED CORRECTLY 2026-09-08, superseding how I phrased it above.

I wrote 'annex the build identity to the REFUSAL, not only to status', which puts the refusal first and would bias an implementation toward treating other surfaces as optional. That is wrong for the case that produced this bead.

THE CORRECT REQUIREMENT: identity must be present on EVERY outcome surface — the refusal, the status read, and the SUCCESSFUL dispatch result alike. The reason is that the incident behind this bead was not a build-identity failure at all. There was no identity anywhere to be wrong. It was a participant that ran a correct, successful dispatch and could not tell afterwards which build had produced the behaviour it observed — and so nearly retracted a correct finding.

A refusal-first design would leave that exact case uncovered, because nothing was refused. 'Identity on every outcome' is the requirement; 'especially on refusals' is a false emphasis that happens to describe only the second-worst symptom.

Clarified by the pi-specialists session, which is the participant it happened to.
source.title: Operator review: surface build identity, explain the lease, state latency, trim rationale
